A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PPD serving system. All 14 pages of v1 and 19 pages of v2, including Appendices A–C, are readable; retained figures, tables, and methods can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original interference microbenchmarks, synthetic serving experiments, ShareGPT/WildChat evaluations, and appendix scaling and failure-rate results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds a three-way WildChat comparison and network-bandwidth emulation results.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same offline weighted TTFT-benefit/TPOT-penalty score, nearest-grid lookup, binary routing decision, and mandatory Turn-1 PD path. The rewritten formulation and newly disclosed discretization thresholds do not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: ShareGPT, WildChat, and the synthetic workload coverage are retained. Section 6.4 adds simulated slower-interconnect scenarios, extending evaluation beyond the original NVLink environment without adding datasets or serving tasks.

E2.justification: Section 6.3, Table 3, and Figure 11 add static x=1 (Full AP-to-D) to the real-world WildChat comparison against PPD and x=0. This comparator existed in v1's synthetic evaluations but was absent from its corresponding real-world comparison.

E3.justification: v2 adds a separate nine-QPS, three-configuration WildChat comparison and bandwidth emulation using calibrated receive-path delays on 500 conversations at QPS=1 and 1P_3D. Appendix C.5 also considers a 10-second timeout versus 30 seconds. The original hardware, models, and synthetic sweep protocol remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 6.4 adds sensitivity testing across four network-speed conditions, and Appendix C.5 reports how tightening the timeout affects stability. The existing concurrency, context-length, turn/model scaling, and routing-weight analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The existing shaded bands and error-bar plots are unchanged. Neither the new comparisons nor the bandwidth study introduces repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance testing.

E6.justification: Important new results address dynamic routing versus always-local routing: Table 3 reports 14/27 TTFT wins for PPD versus 13/27 for x=1, while Figure 11 shows similar end-to-end latency and equal stability. Figure 5 adds PD TTFT increasing from 143.7 to 170.6 ms as bandwidth falls, with PPD near 51 ms. Original plots and tables retain their values. Figure 11's caption reports 13/27 failures, but its plot contains 23 failure markers.

T1.justification: Section 3 removes v1's expected-latency J/argmax formulation and explicitly distinguishes static routing fractions from binary per-request decisions. The replacement uses the score already present in v1's Algorithm 1, correcting the formal framing without introducing a new algorithm or proof.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain unchanged. v2 explicitly confines the introduction's 48–73% reduction claim to synthetic sweeps and replaces the conclusion's Pareto-optimality wording with an offline-tuned routing description and an approximately 68% average reduction on real-world workloads.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands interpretation and applicability boundaries. It explains configuration sizing versus routing-weight tuning, interprets the near-overlap of x=1 and PPD latency curves, and distinguishes transfer-time from queueing benefits. Sections 6.5–7 newly acknowledge that PPD does not enforce end-to-end SLO bounds and that offline calibration becomes suboptimal under hardware or workload drift.

D1.justification: New Appendix B.1 specifies context-bin boundaries at 512 and 4096 tokens and explains request-feature discretization. Appendix B.6 documents delay injection, its formula, and the 128 KiB per-token KV footprint. These expand reproducibility information; the existing session, discovery, and proxy details are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to TetriInfer, Gemini, Parallax, and LoongServe. Discussion more explicitly positions AMPD's online adaptation as complementary to PPD's offline approach and identifies potential integrations. The broader related-work coverage remains intact.

P1.justification: Substantial rewriting affects the introduction and contribution list, Section 3's problem statement, method exposition, discussion, and conclusion. Appendix interpretation is considerably expanded, and new evaluation and implementation subsections reorganize the exposition while retaining the overall section framework.

P2.justification: v2 adds bandwidth Figure 5, three-way comparison Figure 11, and winner-count Table 3. Existing plots are unchanged but some are relocated, renumbered, and recaptioned; Algorithm 1 is condensed. The new Figure 6 caption incorrectly reverses the unchanged plot's left-to-right operating-point order.

improvement.justification: v2 fills the missing real-world x=1 comparison, documents routing thresholds, improves the formal framing, and states meaningful deployment limitations. These make the unchanged method easier to assess and reproduce. The gains are tempered by reporting errors: Figure 11 claims 13 failures despite 23 plotted markers, and Figure 6 reverses its operating-point order in the caption.
